topic: How can real-time traffic be prioritized in dynamic resource allocation without underutilizing satellite capacity during off-peak?
consensus_response: To prioritize real-time traffic in dynamic resource allocation, we can utilize Constantly Assigned Slots (CAS) for high-priority interactive traffic. CAS ensures guaranteed capacity allocation, minimizing latency. In contrast, lower-priority non-interactive traffic can be mapped onto Volume-Based Dynamic Capacity (VBDC) and Free Capacity Allocation (FCA) capacities, optimizing capacity utilization while providing fewer guarantees. The trade-off between fixed allocated capacity and dynamically allocated capacity is critical in satellite communication networks. By incorporating CAS and VBDC/FCA capacities, we can optimize dynamic resource allocation while maintaining QoS guarantees. Additionally, considering the satellite link's physical characteristics and high fixed latencies, we can develop DBA schemes that account for these limitations, ensuring efficient resource utilization.
reference_context: In contrast to terrestrial networks, satellite links require determining actual traffic QoS requirements due to high latencies or jitter values as well as packet losses that cannot be avoided by preventing congestion in the network.
